# Incident Report: STRRAT RAT Infection

**Evidence source:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (only artifact in the evidence directory; no separate IDS/Suricata export was present)
**Capture window:** 2024-07-30 06:38:48 to 06:48:34 (+04:00), ~9m45s, 11,562 frames

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.16.1.66** | Consistent source IP across all traffic below |
| MAC address | **00:1e:64:ec:f3:08** | ARP replies for 172.16.1.66 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** | NBNS name registration, DNS self-registration (`DESKTOP-SKBR25F.wiresharkworkshop.online`), and confirmed independently inside the STRRAT beacon payload |
| AD domain | wiresharkworkshop.online (DC: WIRESHARK-WS-DC, 172.16.1.4) | Kerberos realm `WIRESHARKWORKSHOP.ONLINE`, LDAP/CLDAP/Kerberos traffic to 172.16.1.4 |
| Logged-in user | **ccollier** | Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString: ccollier`; also self-reported inside every STRRAT beacon |
| OS (self-reported by malware) | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit, with Windows Defender active | STRRAT beacon field |

## Malware Family

**STRRAT** (Java-based remote access trojan/credential stealer).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The malware's C2 protocol transmits the literal cleartext string `STRRAT` as a field in every check-in message, e.g.:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|UGljdHVyZXM=|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|1 Sec
```

This is not an inference from behavior alone — the family name is present verbatim in the wire protocol. Additional fields decoded from the stream:
- Client/HWID: `1BE8292C`
- Reported STRRAT build version: `1.6`
- Framing: each message is length-prefixed (`<byte-count>\r\n\r\n` followed by the pipe-delimited payload)
- Beacon interval: ~5 seconds, sustained for the remainder of the capture (411 packets on this stream, first seen at t+76.99s, still running at t+~316s when the capture ends)
- The base64 field is the victim's current foreground window title, decoded across the session to: `Documents`, `Fanad Head Lighthouse - Paint`, `Home`, `Pictures`, `Program Manager` — confirming active window/activity monitoring, a known STRRAT capability, was functioning against the live user session.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` (TCP) — STRRAT C2, custom pipe-delimited plaintext protocol described above. Never resolved via DNS in this capture (the implant connects by hardcoded IP, bypassing DNS-based detection).

**Supporting/secondary infrastructure (behavioral, not C2):**
- `ip-api.com` (208.95.112.1:80) — `GET /json/`, User-Agent `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/73.0.3683.86 Safari/537.36` (a stale/hardcoded Chrome UA, not a real browsing session). This request fires 0.97s after the STRRAT TCP handshake completes and returns victim geolocation (IP 136.49.34.127, Austin, TX, US) — consistent with a malware self-identification/geofencing check, not user activity.

**Malicious/staging domains — no maliciousness observed directly, but timing is significant:**
In the 13 seconds immediately preceding the first STRRAT C2 connection, the host made TLS connections to:
- `github.com` (140.82.113.3) — t+64.05s
- `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133) — t+64.83s, ~833 KB downloaded to the host over 6s
- `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209) — t+68.01s, ~8.9 MB downloaded to the host in 5.8s

STRRAT is a Java-based RAT, and this sequence (GitHub-hosted file, then a large Maven Central transfer, then C2 check-in 9 seconds later) is consistent with a loader staging a JAR payload and/or a Java runtime before executing STRRAT. This is a **behavioral** observation only — these are legitimate CDN/repository hosts, all sessions were TLS-encrypted, and no plaintext content, filenames, or file hashes were recoverable from them in this capture.

**Transferred files / SHA256 hashes:** None recoverable. The only cleartext HTTP objects in the capture are `connecttest.txt` (Microsoft NCSI check) and the `ip-api.com` JSON geolocation response; SMB traffic contained only routine Group Policy files (`Registry.pol`, `GptTmpl.inf`, `gpt.ini`) from the domain controller. No malware binary, JAR, or dropped file was transmitted in the clear anywhere in this capture, so no file names or hashes can be grounded in the evidence.

## Summary

Host DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged on as domain user `ccollier` on the `wiresharkworkshop.online` AD domain, is actively compromised by **STRRAT** (build 1.6, client ID `1BE8292C`). The infection is confirmed by the malware's own protocol literally naming itself in cleartext beacons sent every ~5 seconds to **141.98.10.79:12132**, which also carry live foreground-window telemetry. A GitHub/Maven Central download sequence immediately preceding the first C2 connection is the probable (but TLS-obscured) delivery/staging mechanism. Recommend isolating the host immediately, capturing memory/disk for the STRRAT JAR and persistence artifacts, and blocking 141.98.10.79/12132 at the perimeter.
